This weak tornado took a north-northeast track. It caused minor tree, barn, and shed damage along Highway 171 and FM 3119.
Trees were uprooted and thrown onto cars and houses.
Trees were blown down and a garage door buckled.

A 60 mph wind gust was reported at Highway 171 in Tehuacana.
Significant damage occurred to a house on Lake Mexia when a large tree was uprooted and fell on the house. Trees fell onto a shed as well.
Damage to a corner of a house in the Forest Glade neighborhood was reported. The report was relayed by the media.
Two power poles and several trees were blown down.
Large trees and power lines were blown down in Coolidge and Mexia. Large limbs were blown down near the Forest Glade area. A roof was ripped off a trailer home near Lake Mexia.

Wind gusts up to 60 MPH were reported flowing into a storm west of Mexia.
Large limbs were blown into roadways west of Mexia.
A fireworks stand was blown over with two people inside.
A building at the Prairie Hill Dragway suffered damage and light poles in the area were bent.
A barn was destroyed along Limestone County Road 312. Tree limbs and power lines were also down across the county.
The Cedar Island Ranch on Limestone County Road 198 lost several large cedar trees. Structural damage to a horse barn also occurred.
A 65 MPH wind gust was estimated 4.5 miles north of Mexia on TX HWY 171.
A homeowner suffered damage to his roof when a large limb fell, puncturing a hole into the roof. Several outbuildings were also destroyed on the property.
Large limbs were knocked down and two large barns suffered damage to a roof and sides in the community of Big Hill.
Siding and roof damage was reported to a building along CR 120.
The roofs were damaged on two unoccupied mobile homes north of Coolidge. Other visible damage was sustained to the two mobile homes.
Mexia police officers reported quarter sized hail in town.
Golfball size hail fell on the western side of Mexia.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado occurred approximately 3 miles northeast of Coolidge. This tornado had a path length of approximately 1.3 miles and an estimated width of 100 yards. Mostly tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated at 70 mph.
Golfball size hail fell about one mile west of Wortham.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-1 tornado occurred in Groesbeck. This tornado had a path length of approximately one mile and an estimated width of 75 yards. Tree and building damage was observed along the path, mainly in downtown Groesbeck. The Courthouse, the Dairy Queen, t…

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado began approximately 1.5 miles southwest of Personville. This tornado had a path length of approximately 0.75 miles and an estimated width of 100 yards. Some tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated near 75 mph.

Several medium sized tree limbs were knocked down by strong thunderstorm winds. In addition, a large tree was uprooted and fell into a home. Saturated soils are believed to have contributed to the tree falling over under winds below 60 mph.
A trained spotter reported three power poles down in the city of Thornton, TX. A sheet metal carport was also damaged to the north of Thornton along with some tree branches.
Trees and power lines down along HWY 14 north of Groesbeck and near Fort Parker State Park.

Damage was reported east of Fort Parker State Park along LCRs 406, 456 and 460. An unoccupied trailer was rolled over and destroyed, metal fences and awnings were damaged, large tree limbs were knocked down, and some trees were uprooted in saturated soils.
Large tree limbs were broken along LCR 406 just north of LCR 412.

Large tree blown over onto home at FM 39 and LCR 458, causing significant damage.
Large 2-3 foot plus trees down in multiple locations between Shiloh and Mexia along HWY 39.
